title: "Error Guide"
subtitle: "Every diagnostic of the Synesis compiler, with example, message and fix"
toc-depth: 2

::: {.callout-note}
## Which version this page refers to
The codes, examples and messages below were verified with **synesis 0.16.0**. Each example was compiled, and the message shown is the one the compiler produced.
:::

# How to use this guide {#sec-como-usar}

Each diagnostic has a stable code, such as `SYNESIS_E047`. The letter gives the family: **E** (error), **W** (warning) and **I** (notice). Some `E` codes show as warnings; the severity of each one is in its section.

| Severity | Effect |
|---|---|
| error | stops the export: no JSON, CSV or spreadsheet is written (unless `--force`) |
| error local to an `EXPORT` block | stops only the artifact of that block |
| warning | compilation proceeds; with `--strict`, warnings count as errors |
| notice | only records a fact |

## Message format {#sec-formato}

Messages are one line each, with file, line and column. Paths are relative to the folder of the `.synp`:

```text
annotations.syn:15:1  [ERROR]  Unknown field `extra` in ITEM block
```

The command line does not print the code. There are three ways to see it:

```bash
synesis compile project.synp --diagnostics-json diagnostics.json   # JSON report
synesis-help lookup E047                                            # the entry of one code
synesis-help search "bundle"                                        # search by subject
```

In VS Code the code comes with the diagnostic, together with the full explanation.

## Options that change what shows {#sec-opcoes}

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--check-codes` | lists every code without a concept ([E004](#sec-e004)) instead of the summary ([E090](#sec-e090)) |
| `--strict` | treats warnings as errors; turns on `--check-codes` |
| `--force` | writes the artifacts even with errors |


# Sources and bibliography {#sec-bibliografia}

## E001 — Reference not found in the `.bib` {#sec-e001}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `UnregisteredSource`

The `@bibref` of a block matches no key in the bibliography file.

```synesis
# annotations.syn
SOURCE @silvva2024
END SOURCE

ITEM @silvva2024
    quote: "text"
END ITEM
```

```text
annotations.syn:1:1  [ERROR]  Reference `@silvva2024` not found in the .bib. Suggestions: `@silva2024`
```

**How to fix:** Check the spelling of the key or add the entry to the `.bib`. The message suggests similar keys when there are any.

## E002 — ITEM without a SOURCE {#sec-e002}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `OrphanItem`

An `ITEM` has a `@bibref` with no `SOURCE` block in the same file.

```synesis
# annotations.syn
ITEM @silva2024
    quote: "text"
END ITEM
```

```text
annotations.syn:1:1  [ERROR]  ITEM `@silva2024` has no matching SOURCE in this file
```

**How to fix:** Create the `SOURCE @key` block in the same `.syn`, before the items, or fix the `@bibref` of the ITEM.

## E003 — SOURCE without ITEMs {#sec-e003}

**Severity:** warning · **Class:** `SourceWithoutItems`

A source was registered but none of its excerpts was analysed.

```synesis
# annotations.syn
SOURCE @silva2024
END SOURCE
```

```text
annotations.syn:1:1  [WARNING]  SOURCE `@silva2024` has no associated ITEM
```

**How to fix:** Add at least one `ITEM` or remove the `SOURCE`. It is a warning: compilation proceeds.

## E070 — Duplicate SOURCE {#sec-e070}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `DuplicateSourceBibref`

The same `@bibref` opens two `SOURCE` blocks in the same file.

```synesis
# annotations.syn
SOURCE @silva2024
END SOURCE

ITEM @silva2024
    quote: "Cost limits adoption."
END ITEM

SOURCE @silva2024
END SOURCE
```

```text
annotations.syn:8:1  [ERROR]  SOURCE `@silva2024` duplicated in this file
```

**How to fix:** Keep a single `SOURCE` block per reference; you may have as many `ITEM` blocks as needed.

## E072 — Invalid BibTeX entry {#sec-e072}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `MalformedBibliographyEntry`

An entry of the `.bib` is not valid BibTeX.

```bibtex
% references.bib
@article{silva2024,
    author = {Silva, Ana},
    title = {Study},
    year = {2024}
}

@article{souza2023,
    author = {Souza, Bia},
    title = {Open brace
```

```text
references.bib:1:1  [ERROR]  Entry `@article` in `references.bib` is not valid BibTeX
```

**How to fix:** Fix the indicated entry (opening and closing braces, commas between fields).

## E089 — Duplicate key across files {#sec-e089}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `DuplicateKeyAcrossFiles`

The same key appears in two bibliography (or dataset) files. The first occurrence wins.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "extra.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
END PROJECT
```

```bibtex
% extra.bib
@article{silva2024,
    author = {Silva, Ana},
    title = {Study},
    year = {2024}
}
```

```text
extra.bib:1:1  [ERROR]  Duplicate key `silva2024`: already defined in `references.bib:1`
```

**How to fix:** Decide which record is correct and remove the other.

# Concepts and the organizing model {#sec-ontologia}

## E004 — Code without a concept {#sec-e004}

**Severity:** warning · **Class:** `UndefinedCode`

A code used in a `CODE` field or in a chain has no `ONTOLOGY` block. The per-occurrence check is optional: it shows with `--check-codes` or `--strict` (see E090).

```synesis
# annotations.syn
SOURCE @silva2024
END SOURCE

ITEM @silva2024
    quote: "text"
    code: Costs
END ITEM
```

```synesis
# ontology.syno
ONTOLOGY Cost
    definition: Cost.
END ONTOLOGY
```

```text
annotations.syn:4:1  [WARNING]  Code `Costs` is not defined in the organizing model. Suggested fix -> `Cost`
```

**How to fix:** Define the concept in a `.syno` file or fix the spelling of the code. The message suggests the closest concept.

## E090 — Summary of codes without a concept {#sec-e090}

**Severity:** warning · **Class:** `UndefinedCodesSummary`

With the per-occurrence check off (the default), the compiler emits a single line with the number of codes without a concept.

```synesis
# annotations.syn
SOURCE @silva2024
END SOURCE

ITEM @silva2024
    quote: "text"
    code: Costs, Trust
END ITEM
```

```text
project.synp:1:1  [WARNING]  2 code(s) without a concept in the organizing model (2 occurrence(s)); use --check-codes to list them
```

**How to fix:** Use `synesis compile --check-codes` to list every occurrence. Before the ontology exists, this warning is expected.

## E005 — ONTOLOGY without `ONTOLOGY FIELDS` {#sec-e005}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `OntologyWithoutTemplateFields`

The project has `ONTOLOGY` blocks but the template does not declare which fields they accept.

```synesis
# template.synt
TEMPLATE demo

ITEM FIELDS
    REQUIRED quote
END ITEM FIELDS

FIELD quote TYPE QUOTATION
    SCOPE ITEM
END FIELD
```

```synesis
# ontology.syno
ONTOLOGY Cost
    definition: Cost.
END ONTOLOGY
```

```text
project.synp:1:1  [ERROR]  Project has ONTOLOGY blocks but the template does not declare ONTOLOGY FIELDS
```

**How to fix:** Add the `ONTOLOGY FIELDS` block to the template, with the corresponding `FIELD` definitions.

## E068 — Duplicate concept {#sec-e068}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `DuplicateOntologyConcept`

Two `ONTOLOGY` blocks define the same concept (the comparison ignores case), in the same file or in different files.

```synesis
# ontology.syno
ONTOLOGY Cost
    definition: Cost.
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY cost
    definition: cost.
END ONTOLOGY
```

```text
ontology.syno:5:1  [ERROR]  Concept `cost` duplicated in ontology.syno and ontology.syno
```

**How to fix:** Merge the two definitions into one block. If they are distinct concepts, rename one of them.

## E103 — Names colliding after Unicode normalization {#sec-e103}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `IdentityCollision`

Two names look different in the file (composed and decomposed characters) but have the same identity after NFC normalization.

```text
ontology.syno:5:1  [ERROR]  Concepts `Café_Culture` and `Café_Culture` collide (same identity after Unicode normalization)
```

**How to fix:** Write the name always the same way; delete one of the blocks.

## W071 — Identical definitions {#sec-w071}

**Severity:** warning · **Class:** `DuplicateOntologyDescription`

Two concepts have the same description, a frequent sign of a conceptual duplicate.

```synesis
# ontology.syno
ONTOLOGY Cost
    description: Financial barrier.
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY Price
    description: Financial barrier.
END ONTOLOGY
```

```text
ontology.syno:5:1  [WARNING]  Concepts `Cost` and `Price` have identical descriptions
```

**How to fix:** Differentiate the definitions or consolidate the concepts (see `ROLE USE`).

# Chains and relations {#sec-chains}

A **qualified** chain alternates concepts and relations (`A -> RELATION -> B`) and requires the `RELATIONS` block in the template. A **simple** chain has only concepts (`A -> B`).

## E007 — Arity not met {#sec-e007}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `ChainArityViolation`

The chain has fewer concepts than the `ARITY` of the field requires.

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD chain TYPE CHAIN
    SCOPE ITEM
    ARITY >= 3
    RELATIONS
        ENABLES: makes possible
        INHIBITS: limits
    END RELATIONS
END FIELD
```

```synesis
# annotations.syn
SOURCE @silva2024
END SOURCE

ITEM @silva2024
    quote: "text"
    chain: Cost -> INHIBITS -> Adoption
END ITEM
```

```text
annotations.syn:6:5  [ERROR]  Chain with 2 element(s), the template requires >= 3
```

**How to fix:** Complete the chain or revise `ARITY` in the template.

## E008 — Named relations in a field without `RELATIONS` {#sec-e008}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `QualifiedChainWithoutRelations`

The chain uses relation names but the field declares no `RELATIONS`. The compiler reads an upper-case middle element as a relation.

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD chain TYPE CHAIN
    SCOPE ITEM
    ARITY >= 2
END FIELD
```

```synesis
# annotations.syn
SOURCE @silva2024
END SOURCE

ITEM @silva2024
    quote: "text"
    chain: Cost -> INHIBITS -> Adoption
END ITEM
```

```text
annotations.syn:6:5  [ERROR]  Chain with named relations in `chain`, but the template defines no RELATIONS
```

**How to fix:** Declare `RELATIONS` in the field or write a simple chain (`A -> B`).

## E009 — Simple chain where relations are required {#sec-e009}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `SimpleChainWithRelationsRequired`

The field declares `RELATIONS` but the chain names none.

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD chain TYPE CHAIN
    SCOPE ITEM
    ARITY >= 2
    RELATIONS
        ENABLES: makes possible
        INHIBITS: limits
    END RELATIONS
END FIELD
```

```synesis
# annotations.syn
SOURCE @silva2024
END SOURCE

ITEM @silva2024
    quote: "text"
    chain: Cost -> Adoption
END ITEM
```

```text
annotations.syn:6:5  [ERROR]  Simple chain in `chain` but the template requires named relations
```

**How to fix:** Insert a declared relation between the concepts.

## E010 — Undeclared relation {#sec-e010}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `InvalidChainRelation`

The chain uses a relation that is not in the `RELATIONS` of the field.

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD chain TYPE CHAIN
    SCOPE ITEM
    ARITY >= 2
    RELATIONS
        ENABLES: makes possible
        INHIBITS: limits
    END RELATIONS
END FIELD
```

```synesis
# annotations.syn
SOURCE @silva2024
END SOURCE

ITEM @silva2024
    quote: "text"
    chain: Cost -> BLOCKS -> Adoption
END ITEM
```

```text
annotations.syn:6:5  [ERROR]  Relation `BLOCKS` not declared in the template
```

**How to fix:** Use a declared relation or add the new one to the template, with its description.

## E011 — Malformed qualified chain {#sec-e011}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `MalformedQualifiedChain`

The concept → relation → concept alternation is broken; for instance, the chain ends with a relation.

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD chain TYPE CHAIN
    SCOPE ITEM
    ARITY >= 2
    RELATIONS
        ENABLES: makes possible
        INHIBITS: limits
    END RELATIONS
END FIELD
```

```synesis
# annotations.syn
SOURCE @silva2024
END SOURCE

ITEM @silva2024
    quote: "text"
    chain: Cost -> INHIBITS -> Adoption -> ENABLES
END ITEM
```

```text
annotations.syn:6:5  [ERROR]  Qualified chain with incorrect structure: Cost -> INHIBITS -> Adoption -> ENABLES
```

**How to fix:** Keep an odd number of elements: concept, relation, concept.

## E013 — Chain without the `->` operator {#sec-e013}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `ChainWithoutArrowOperator`

The value of a `CHAIN` field is a single element, with no `->`. A line with several elements and no arrow usually shows as E028.

**How to fix:** Link at least two concepts with `->`.

## E014 — Concept named like a relation {#sec-e014}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `ConceptNameMatchesRelation`

A concept in a code position has the same name as a declared relation.

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD chain TYPE CHAIN
    SCOPE ITEM
    ARITY >= 2
    RELATIONS
        ENABLES: makes possible
        INHIBITS: limits
    END RELATIONS
END FIELD
```

```synesis
# annotations.syn
SOURCE @silva2024
END SOURCE

ITEM @silva2024
    quote: "text"
    chain: ENABLES -> INHIBITS -> Adoption
END ITEM
```

```text
annotations.syn:6:5  [ERROR]  `ENABLES` is ambiguous: both concept and relation in `chain`
```

**How to fix:** Rename the concept or the relation.

## E015 — Concept with spaces {#sec-e015}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `ConceptWithSpaces`

A chain concept contains spaces.

```synesis
# annotations.syn
SOURCE @silva2024
END SOURCE

ITEM @silva2024
    quote: "text"
    chain: Public Acceptance -> ENABLES -> Adoption
END ITEM
```

```text
annotations.syn:6:5  [ERROR]  Concept `Public Acceptance` contains spaces. Suggested fix -> `Public_Acceptance`
```

**How to fix:** Use underscores or CamelCase: `Public_Acceptance`.

# Bundles {#sec-bundles}

A `BUNDLE` groups fields that only make sense together and pairs them by position inside the ITEM.

## E016 — Missing bundle member {#sec-e016}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `MissingBundleField`

A bundle field appears without its partner, or a required bundle is absent.

```synesis
# template.synt
ITEM FIELDS
    REQUIRED quote
    REQUIRED BUNDLE note, chain
END ITEM FIELDS
```

```synesis
# annotations.syn
SOURCE @silva2024
END SOURCE

ITEM @silva2024
    quote: "text"
    note: Cost is a barrier
END ITEM
```

```text
annotations.syn:4:1  [ERROR]  Bundle (note, chain): missing fields `chain`
```

**How to fix:** Write every field of the bundle.

## E017 — Unequal bundle counts {#sec-e017}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `BundleCountMismatch`

The bundle fields occur in different numbers.

```synesis
# template.synt
ITEM FIELDS
    REQUIRED quote
    REQUIRED BUNDLE note, chain
END ITEM FIELDS
```

```synesis
# annotations.syn
SOURCE @silva2024
END SOURCE

ITEM @silva2024
    quote: "text"
    note: Cost is a barrier
    chain: Cost -> INHIBITS -> Adoption
    note: Trust helps
END ITEM
```

```text
annotations.syn:4:1  [ERROR]  Bundle (note, chain) with unequal counts: note=2, chain=1
```

**How to fix:** Each occurrence of a field needs its partner, in the same order.

## E018 — Single-field bundle {#sec-e018}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `SingleFieldBundle`

The template declares a bundle with only one field.

```synesis
# template.synt
ITEM FIELDS
    REQUIRED BUNDLE quote
END ITEM FIELDS
```

```text
template.synt:7:1  [ERROR]  Bundle `quote` declared with only one field in the template
```

**How to fix:** Declare at least two fields, or use a plain `REQUIRED`/`OPTIONAL`.

# Field presence {#sec-presenca}

## E020 — Missing required field {#sec-e020}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `MissingRequiredField`

A field listed as `REQUIRED` for that block type (SOURCE, ITEM or ONTOLOGY) is missing.

```synesis
# template.synt
ITEM FIELDS
    REQUIRED quote, code
END ITEM FIELDS
```

```synesis
# annotations.syn
SOURCE @silva2024
END SOURCE

ITEM @silva2024
    quote: "text"
END ITEM
```

```text
annotations.syn:4:1  [ERROR]  Required field `code` missing in ITEM block
```

**How to fix:** Fill in the field, or make it `OPTIONAL` in the template.

## E021 — Forbidden field present {#sec-e021}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `ForbiddenFieldPresent`

The block fills in a field listed as `FORBIDDEN`.

```synesis
# template.synt
ITEM FIELDS
    REQUIRED quote
    FORBIDDEN note
END ITEM FIELDS
```

```synesis
# annotations.syn
SOURCE @silva2024
END SOURCE

ITEM @silva2024
    quote: "text"
    note: x
END ITEM
```

```text
annotations.syn:4:1  [ERROR]  Forbidden field `note` in ITEM block — remove this line
```

**How to fix:** Remove the line.

## E022 — Unknown field {#sec-e022}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `UnknownFieldName`

The file uses a field the template does not define for that scope.

```synesis
# template.synt
ITEM FIELDS
    REQUIRED quote
END ITEM FIELDS
```

```synesis
# annotations.syn
SOURCE @silva2024
END SOURCE

ITEM @silva2024
    quote: "text"
    citation: x
END ITEM
```

```text
annotations.syn:4:1  [ERROR]  Unknown field `citation` in ITEM block
```

**How to fix:** Fix the name, or declare the `FIELD` and list it in the `FIELDS` block of the scope.

## E023 — Empty ITEM {#sec-e023}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `EmptyItemBlock`

An `ITEM` block has no field at all.

```synesis
# annotations.syn
SOURCE @silva2024
END SOURCE

ITEM @silva2024
END ITEM
```

```text
annotations.syn:4:1  [ERROR]  Empty ITEM block — no fields
```

**How to fix:** Fill in the block or remove it.

# Values and field types {#sec-valores}

## E026 — Decimal in an integer `SCALE` {#sec-e026}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `DecimalInIntegerScale`

The `FORMAT` of the field uses integer bounds and the value has decimals.

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD confidence TYPE SCALE
    SCOPE ITEM
    FORMAT [1..5]
END FIELD
```

```synesis
# annotations.syn
SOURCE @silva2024
END SOURCE

ITEM @silva2024
    quote: "text"
    confidence: 3.5
END ITEM
```

```text
annotations.syn:4:1  [ERROR]  Decimal value `3.5` in `confidence` — the field only accepts integers [1..5]
```

**How to fix:** Use an integer, or rescale the field (for example `[0..2]` instead of 0, 0.5 and 1). Decimals are accepted only when at least one `FORMAT` bound is not a whole number, as in `[0..5.5]`; writing `[1.0..5.0]` is not enough, despite what the diagnostic message suggests.

## E027 — Value outside the `ENUMERATED` list {#sec-e027}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `InvalidEnumeratedValue`

The value is not in the `VALUES` block.

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD status TYPE ENUMERATED
    SCOPE ITEM
    VALUES
        Asserted: stated as fact
        Negated: stated as not holding
    END VALUES
END FIELD
```

```synesis
# annotations.syn
SOURCE @silva2024
END SOURCE

ITEM @silva2024
    quote: "text"
    status: Maybe
END ITEM
```

```text
annotations.syn:4:1  [ERROR]  Invalid value `Maybe` for `status`
```

**How to fix:** Use one of the declared values.

## E028 — Incompatible value type {#sec-e028}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `InvalidFieldType`

The value does not have the form the field type requires (for instance, text where a number is expected).

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD confidence TYPE SCALE
    SCOPE ITEM
    FORMAT [1..5]
END FIELD
```

```synesis
# annotations.syn
SOURCE @silva2024
END SOURCE

ITEM @silva2024
    quote: "text"
    confidence: high
END ITEM
```

```text
annotations.syn:4:1  [ERROR]  Invalid type in `confidence`: expected number, found str
```

**How to fix:** Write the value in the form of the declared type.

## E029 — Unknown value in `ORDERED` {#sec-e029}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `InvalidOrderedValue`

The value matches no declared position.

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD level TYPE ORDERED
    SCOPE ITEM
    VALUES
        [1] Low: marginal
        [2] Medium: relevant
        [3] High: central
    END VALUES
END FIELD
```

```synesis
# annotations.syn
SOURCE @silva2024
END SOURCE

ITEM @silva2024
    quote: "text"
    level: 7
END ITEM
```

```text
annotations.syn:4:1  [ERROR]  Invalid value `7` for `level` (ordered)
```

**How to fix:** Write one of the declared indices.

## E088 — `ORDERED` written with the label {#sec-e088}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `OrderedValueAsLabel`

In an `ORDERED` field the stored datum is the **index**; the label is for display only.

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD level TYPE ORDERED
    SCOPE ITEM
    VALUES
        [1] Low: marginal
        [2] Medium: relevant
        [3] High: central
    END VALUES
END FIELD
```

```synesis
# annotations.syn
SOURCE @silva2024
END SOURCE

ITEM @silva2024
    quote: "text"
    level: High
END ITEM
```

```text
annotations.syn:4:1  [ERROR]  `level: High` — in ORDERED write the index (3); the label is display only
```

**How to fix:** Replace the label with the index the message points to.

## E030 — Value outside the `SCALE` range {#sec-e030}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `ScaleOutOfRange`

The number is outside `[min..max]`.

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD confidence TYPE SCALE
    SCOPE ITEM
    FORMAT [1..5]
END FIELD
```

```synesis
# annotations.syn
SOURCE @silva2024
END SOURCE

ITEM @silva2024
    quote: "text"
    confidence: 9
END ITEM
```

```text
annotations.syn:4:1  [ERROR]  Value `9.0` outside the range [1.0..5.0] in the field `confidence`
```

**How to fix:** Fix the value or the `FORMAT`.

## W031 — Code repeated in the same occurrence {#sec-w031}

**Severity:** warning · **Class:** `DuplicateCodeInField`

The same code appears twice in the same line of a `CODE` field.

```synesis
# annotations.syn
SOURCE @silva2024
END SOURCE

ITEM @silva2024
    quote: "text"
    code: Cost, Cost
END ITEM
```

```text
annotations.syn:4:1  [WARNING]  Code `Cost` duplicated in the field `code`
```

**How to fix:** Remove the repetition.

## E032 — `TOPIC` with spaces {#sec-e032}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `TopicWithSpaces`

A `TOPIC` value is a single term.

```synesis
# ontology.syno
ONTOLOGY Cost
    topic: Social Factors
END ONTOLOGY
```

```text
ontology.syno:1:1  [ERROR]  Value `Social Factors` in `topic` contains spaces. Suggested fix -> `Social_Factors`
```

**How to fix:** Use underscores: `Social_Factors`.

## E033 — Invalid character in an identifier {#sec-e033}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `InvalidIdentifierCharacter`

The name of a code or concept contains a character that is not allowed.

```synesis
# annotations.syn
SOURCE @silva2024
END SOURCE

ITEM @silva2024
    quote: "text"
    code: Cost?
END ITEM
```

```text
annotations.syn:4:1  [ERROR]  Identifier `Cost?` contains the invalid character `?`
```

**How to fix:** Use letters, digits, `_` and `-`.

# Template declaration {#sec-template}

## E039 — Listed field without a definition {#sec-e039}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `UndefinedFieldInScopeFields`

A name appears in a `FIELDS` block but there is no `FIELD` with that name.

```synesis
# template.synt
ITEM FIELDS
    REQUIRED quote, country
END ITEM FIELDS
```

```text
template.synt:1:1  [ERROR]  Field `country` listed in `ITEM FIELDS` without a FIELD definition
```

**How to fix:** Define the `FIELD` or remove the name from the list.

## E042 — Defined field never listed {#sec-e042}

**Severity:** warning · **Class:** `OrphanFieldDefinition`

A `FIELD` is used by no `FIELDS` block.

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD note TYPE MEMO
    SCOPE ITEM
END FIELD
```

```text
template.synt:7:1  [WARNING]  Field `note` defined but missing from `ITEM FIELDS`
```

**How to fix:** List the field in the block of its scope or delete the definition.

## E006 — Scope mismatch {#sec-e006}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `FieldScopeListMismatch`

The field is listed in the block of one scope but its `SCOPE` is another.

```synesis
# template.synt
ITEM FIELDS
    REQUIRED quote
    OPTIONAL note
END ITEM FIELDS
```

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD note TYPE MEMO
    SCOPE SOURCE
END FIELD
```

```text
template.synt:8:1  [ERROR]  Field `note` listed in `ITEM FIELDS` but its declared SCOPE is SOURCE
```

**How to fix:** Make the `SCOPE` and the `FIELDS` block agree.

## E047 — `CHAIN` without `ARITY` {#sec-e047}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `ChainWithoutArity`

Every `CHAIN` field declares the minimum number of concepts.

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD chain TYPE CHAIN
    SCOPE ITEM
END FIELD
```

```text
template.synt:8:1  [ERROR]  Field `chain` (CHAIN) without an ARITY declaration in the template
```

**How to fix:** Add, for instance, `ARITY >= 2`.

## E048 — `ARITY` incompatible with `RELATIONS` {#sec-e048}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `ArityRelationsMismatch`

The arity asks for more links than the declared relations can form.

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD chain TYPE CHAIN
    SCOPE ITEM
    ARITY >= 4
    RELATIONS
        ENABLES: makes possible
    END RELATIONS
END FIELD
```

```text
template.synt:8:1  [ERROR]  Field `chain`: ARITY >= 4 requires more relations than the 1 declared
```

**How to fix:** Declare more relations or lower the arity.

## E049 — `ORDERED` without `VALUES` {#sec-e049}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `OrderedWithoutValues`

An `ORDERED` field needs its options, in order.

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD level TYPE ORDERED
    SCOPE ITEM
END FIELD
```

```text
template.synt:7:1  [ERROR]  Field `level` (ORDERED) without a VALUES block in the template
```

**How to fix:** Add the `VALUES` block with `[N]` indices.

## E050 — `ENUMERATED` without `VALUES` {#sec-e050}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `EnumeratedWithoutValues`

An `ENUMERATED` field needs the closed list of values.

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD status TYPE ENUMERATED
    SCOPE ITEM
END FIELD
```

```text
template.synt:7:1  [ERROR]  Field `status` (ENUMERATED) without a VALUES block in the template
```

**How to fix:** Add the `VALUES` block.

## E051 — `SCALE` without `FORMAT` {#sec-e051}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `ScaleWithoutFormat`

A `SCALE` field needs the numeric range.

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD confidence TYPE SCALE
    SCOPE ITEM
END FIELD
```

```text
template.synt:7:1  [ERROR]  Field `confidence` (SCALE) without a FORMAT declaration in the template
```

**How to fix:** Add, for instance, `FORMAT [1..5]`.

## E052 — Invalid `FORMAT` syntax {#sec-e052}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `InvalidFormatSyntax`

The `FORMAT` of a `SCALE` field does not have the form `[min..max]`.

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD confidence TYPE SCALE
    SCOPE ITEM
    FORMAT percent
END FIELD
```

```text
template.synt:7:1  [ERROR]  Invalid FORMAT in `confidence`: `percent` — use `[min..max]`
```

**How to fix:** Write `FORMAT [min..max]`.

## E053 — Invalid `ARITY` operator {#sec-e053}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `InvalidArityOperator`

The accepted operators are `>=`, `>`, `<=`, `<` and `=`. Other spellings usually produce a syntax error first.

**How to fix:** Use one of the accepted operators.

## E054 — `FORMAT` outside `SCALE` {#sec-e054}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `FormatOnNonScale`

`FORMAT` only applies to `SCALE` fields.

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD note TYPE TEXT
    SCOPE ITEM
    FORMAT [1..5]
END FIELD
```

```text
template.synt:7:1  [ERROR]  FORMAT declared in `note` (type TEXT) — FORMAT is exclusive to SCALE
```

**How to fix:** Remove the line or change the type.

## E055 — `ARITY` outside `CHAIN` {#sec-e055}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `ArityOnNonChain`

`ARITY` only applies to `CHAIN` fields.

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD note TYPE MEMO
    SCOPE ITEM
    ARITY >= 2
END FIELD
```

```text
template.synt:7:1  [ERROR]  ARITY declared in `note` (type MEMO) — ARITY is exclusive to CHAIN
```

**How to fix:** Remove the line or change the type.

## E056 — `RELATIONS` outside `CHAIN` {#sec-e056}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `RelationsOnNonChain`

`RELATIONS` only applies to `CHAIN` fields.

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD note TYPE TEXT
    SCOPE ITEM
    RELATIONS
        ENABLES: makes possible
    END RELATIONS
END FIELD
```

```text
template.synt:7:1  [ERROR]  RELATIONS declared in `note` (type TEXT) — RELATIONS is exclusive to CHAIN
```

**How to fix:** Remove the block or change the type.

## E086 — `VALUES` outside `ORDERED`/`ENUMERATED` {#sec-e086}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `ValuesOnNonEnumerable`

In any other type the list would be ignored, so it is refused.

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD note TYPE TEXT
    SCOPE ITEM
    VALUES
        High: high
    END VALUES
END FIELD
```

```text
template.synt:7:1  [ERROR]  VALUES declared in `note` (type TEXT) — VALUES is exclusive to ORDERED/ENUMERATED
```

**How to fix:** Remove the `VALUES` block or change the type.

## E087 — `[N]` index in `ENUMERATED` {#sec-e087}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `IndexOnEnumeratedValue`

The index establishes order, and `ENUMERATED` has none.

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD status TYPE ENUMERATED
    SCOPE ITEM
    VALUES
        [1] Asserted: stated as fact
        [2] Negated: stated as not holding
    END VALUES
END FIELD
```

```text
template.synt:7:1  [ERROR]  `[N]` prefix in the VALUES of `status` (ENUMERATED type) — the index is exclusive to ORDERED
```

**How to fix:** Remove the prefix, or use `ORDERED` if the order is intended.

## E057 — Duplicate `FIELDS` block {#sec-e057}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `DuplicateScopeBlock`

There are two `FIELDS` blocks for the same scope. In version 0.16.0 the compiler does not emit this diagnostic: repeated blocks are accepted silently.

**How to fix:** Merge the lists into a single block.

## E058 — Value with leading or trailing whitespace {#sec-e058}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `ValueWithWhitespace`

A value of the `VALUES` block has whitespace at the start or end. With the current template syntax the space is usually stripped while reading, so this is rare.

**How to fix:** Remove the extra whitespace.

## E059 — Duplicate value in `VALUES` {#sec-e059}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `DuplicateValue`

The same value appears twice in the list.

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD status TYPE ENUMERATED
    SCOPE ITEM
    VALUES
        Active: in use
        Active: repeated
    END VALUES
END FIELD
```

```text
template.synt:11:9  [ERROR]  Duplicate value `Active` in the VALUES block of `status`
```

**How to fix:** Keep a single entry.

## E060 — Non-integer `ARITY` {#sec-e060}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `NonIntegerArityValue`

The number of `ARITY` must be an integer.

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD chain TYPE CHAIN
    SCOPE ITEM
    ARITY >= 2.0
END FIELD
```

```text
template.synt:8:1  [ERROR]  ARITY of field `chain` uses non-integer value `2.0` — use an integer (e.g. 2)
```

**How to fix:** Write `2`, not `2.0`.

## E069 — Field defined twice {#sec-e069}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `DuplicateFieldName`

Two `FIELD` definitions share a name.

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD note TYPE MEMO
    SCOPE ITEM
END FIELD

FIELD note TYPE MEMO
    SCOPE ITEM
END FIELD
```

```text
template.synt:11:1  [ERROR]  Field `note` defined more than once in the template
```

**How to fix:** Remove or rename one of them.

# Project structure {#sec-projeto}

## E061 — `.syn` file not included {#sec-e061}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `MissingAnnotationsInclude`

A `.syn` in the project folder is reached by no `INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS`.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:1:1  [ERROR]  File `forgotten.syn` not included by INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS in the .synp
```

**How to fix:** Declare the file (or folder) in the `.synp`, or move it out of the project.

## E062 — `.syno` file not included {#sec-e062}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `MissingOntologyInclude`

A `.syno` in the project folder is reached by no `INCLUDE ONTOLOGY`.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:1:1  [ERROR]  File `forgotten.syno` not included by INCLUDE ONTOLOGY in the .synp
```

**How to fix:** Declare the file in the `.synp` or move it.

## E063 — Bibliography not found {#sec-e063}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `MissingBibliographyFile`

The file, folder or pattern of `INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY` finds no `.bib`.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "missing.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:3:5  [ERROR]  References file `missing.bib` declared in the project was not found
```

**How to fix:** Check the path, which is relative to the folder of the `.synp`.

## E064 — Template or project not found {#sec-e064}

**Severity:** error (warning in the editor when there is no `.synp`) · **Class:** `InvalidProjectFile`, `MissingProjectFile`, `MissingTemplateFile`

Code `E064` covers three situations: a declared template that does not exist, no `.synp` in the workspace (in the editor) and a `.synp` with a syntax error.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "missing.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:1:1  [ERROR]  Template `missing.synt` not found
```

**How to fix:** Check the `TEMPLATE` path and the syntax of the `.synp`.

## E065 — Project without `TEMPLATE` {#sec-e065}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `MissingTemplateDeclaration`

The `PROJECT` block declares no template. On the command line, version 0.16.0 usually reports this case as E064.

**How to fix:** Add `TEMPLATE "file.synt"`.

## E066 — Two `PROJECT` blocks {#sec-e066}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `DuplicateProjectBlock`

A `.synp` accepts a single `PROJECT` block.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
END PROJECT

PROJECT other
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:8:1  [ERROR]  Two PROJECT blocks in the same .synp — remove the duplicate
```

**How to fix:** Remove the extra block.

## W067 — `modified` earlier than `created` {#sec-w067}

**Severity:** warning · **Class:** `ModifiedBeforeCreated`

The dates of the `METADATA` block are reversed.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    METADATA
        version: 1.0
        author: Team
        created: 2026-03-01
        modified: 2026-01-01
    END METADATA
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:1:1  [WARNING]  MODIFIED `2026-01-01` e anterior a CREATED `2026-03-01` no METADATA
```

**How to fix:** Fix the dates.

# Files and paths {#sec-caminhos}

Paths in the `.synp` are relative to its folder. For safety, the compiler only reads files in that folder and below; the only exception is `INCLUDE SHARED ONTOLOGY`.

## E073 — Annotations file not found {#sec-e073}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `MissingAnnotationsFile`

`INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS` points to something that does not exist.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "missing.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:5:5  [ERROR]  Annotations file `missing.syn` declared in the project was not found
```

**How to fix:** Check the name and the path.

## E074 — Ontology file not found {#sec-e074}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `MissingOntologyFile`

`INCLUDE ONTOLOGY` points to something that does not exist.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "missing.syno"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:5:5  [ERROR]  Organizing model file `missing.syno` declared in the project was not found
```

**How to fix:** Check the path. An empty `.syno` is valid, but it must exist.

## E075 — Path outside the project {#sec-e075}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `IncludePathEscapesProject`

A path (literal or glob) leaves the project folder.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "../shared.syno"
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:6:5  [ERROR]  Path `../shared.syno` points outside the project folder
```

**How to fix:** Move the file inside the project. For a vocabulary shared by several projects, use `INCLUDE SHARED ONTOLOGY`.

## E076 — Included file unreadable {#sec-e076}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `UnreadableIncludedFile`

The file exists but cannot be read: syntax error, invalid encoding or size above 32 MB.

```synesis
# annotations.syn
SOURCE @silva2024
END SOURCE

ITEM @silva2024
    quote: "text"
```

```text
annotations.syn:1:1  [ERROR]  File `annotations.syn` could not be read: error: annotations.syn:1:1: Unexpected token <EOF> END SOURCE Expected: END
```

**How to fix:** Open the indicated file and fix the problem described in the message.

## E084 — `SHARED` outside `ONTOLOGY` {#sec-e084}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `SharedOnlyForOntology`

`INCLUDE SHARED` is only accepted for ontologies.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE SHARED BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:3:5  [ERROR]  `INCLUDE SHARED` invalid for BIBLIOGRAPHY — only ONTOLOGY accepts SHARED
```

**How to fix:** Copy the file into the project and use a plain `INCLUDE`.

# Linking projects and datasets {#sec-ligacao}

Diagnostics E081, E082 and W083 only appear in the link step, when two or more projects are compiled together. See [How to Link Independent Projects](../howto/ligar_projetos.qmd).

## E077 — Duplicate identity value {#sec-e077}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `DuplicateIdentityValue`

Two `SOURCE` blocks hold the same value in an `IDENTIFIES` field, which acts as a primary key.

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD researcher_id TYPE TEXT
    SCOPE SOURCE
    IDENTIFIES researcher
END FIELD
```

```synesis
# annotations.syn
SOURCE @silva2024
    researcher_id: 001
END SOURCE

ITEM @silva2024
    quote: "a"
END ITEM

SOURCE @souza2023
    researcher_id: 001
END SOURCE

ITEM @souza2023
    quote: "b"
END ITEM
```

```text
annotations.syn:9:1  [ERROR]  Value `1` of `researcher_id` (IDENTIFIES researcher) duplicated in `@silva2024` and `@souza2023`
```

**How to fix:** Each value identifies a single `SOURCE`: fix the data.

## E078 — Linkage modifier outside `SOURCE` {#sec-e078}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `LinkageModifierOutsideSource`

`IDENTIFIES` and `REFERS TO` only apply to `SCOPE SOURCE` fields.

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD author_id TYPE TEXT
    SCOPE ITEM
    REFERS TO researcher
END FIELD
```

```text
template.synt:7:1  [ERROR]  `REFERS TO` in `author_id` (SCOPE ITEM) — only valid in SCOPE SOURCE
```

**How to fix:** Move the field to the `SOURCE` scope.

## E079 — Value missing in the `.bib` {#sec-e079}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `MissingBibliographyValue`

A `REQUIRED ... ON BIBLIOGRAPHY` field has no value in the entry of the `SOURCE`.

```synesis
# template.synt
SOURCE FIELDS
    REQUIRED orcid ON BIBLIOGRAPHY
END SOURCE FIELDS

ITEM FIELDS
    REQUIRED quote
END ITEM FIELDS
```

```bibtex
% references.bib
@article{silva2024,
    author = {Silva, Ana},
    title = {Study},
    year = {2024}
}
```

```text
annotations.syn:1:1  [ERROR]  Field `orcid` (ON BIBLIOGRAPHY) missing in the .bib entry of `@silva2024`
```

**How to fix:** Add the field to the BibTeX entry.

## I080 — External reference declared {#sec-i080}

**Severity:** notice · **Class:** `ExternalReferenceDeclared`

The project declares `REFERS TO` and was compiled alone. It is informational: neither error nor warning.

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD author_id TYPE TEXT
    SCOPE SOURCE
    REFERS TO researcher
END FIELD
```

```text
template.synt:11:1  [INFO]  External reference `researcher` (REFERS TO in author_id) — not materialized in isolation
```

**How to fix:** Nothing to do. To materialize the links, compile together with the project that declares `IDENTIFIES`.

## E081 — Entity with two owners {#sec-e081}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `DuplicateEntityOwner`

Two projects declare `IDENTIFIES` for the same entity label.

```synesis
# lattes.synt
FIELD rid TYPE TEXT
    SCOPE SOURCE
    IDENTIFIES researcher
END FIELD
```

```synesis
# orcid.synt
FIELD rid TYPE TEXT
    SCOPE SOURCE
    IDENTIFIES researcher
END FIELD
```

```text
<link>:0:0  [ERROR]  Entity `researcher` with a duplicate owner: `lattes` and `orcid`
```

**How to fix:** Choose the owner project; in the others use `REFERS TO`.

## E082 — Diverging types in the link {#sec-e082}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `TypeMismatchInLinkage`

The fields linked to the same entity have different `TYPE`.

```synesis
# lattes.synt
FIELD rid TYPE TEXT
    SCOPE SOURCE
    IDENTIFIES researcher
END FIELD
```

```synesis
# papers.synt
FIELD author_id TYPE SCALE
    FORMAT [0..999]
    SCOPE SOURCE
    REFERS TO researcher
END FIELD
```

```text
<link>:0:0  [ERROR]  Tipos divergentes na entidade `researcher`: `lattes` TYPE TEXT vs `papers` TYPE SCALE
```

**How to fix:** Use the same `TYPE` on both sides.

## W083 — Orphan reference {#sec-w083}

**Severity:** warning · **Class:** `OrphanReference`

A `REFERS TO` value matches no `IDENTIFIES`. If it would match ignoring case, the message reports the near-match. The compiler never merges entities.

```synesis
# lattes.syn
SOURCE @lattes1
    rid: A01
END SOURCE

ITEM @lattes1
    quote: "x"
END ITEM
```

```synesis
# papers.syn
SOURCE @papers1
    author_id: a01
END SOURCE

ITEM @papers1
    quote: "x"
END ITEM
```

```text
<link>:0:0  [WARNING]  Orphan REFERS TO `a01` (researcher) — near match `A01` (differs only in case)
```

**How to fix:** Fix the spelling at the source. Orphans can be normal in real corpora.

## E085 — Value missing in the dataset {#sec-e085}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `MissingDatasetValue`

A `REQUIRED ... ON DATASET` field has no value in the TOML record of the `SOURCE`.

```synesis
# template.synt
SOURCE FIELDS
    REQUIRED interview ON DATASET "interview.id"
    REQUIRED region ON DATASET "interview.region"
END SOURCE FIELDS

ITEM FIELDS
    REQUIRED quote
END ITEM FIELDS
```

```toml
# records/s1.toml
[interview]
id = "silva2024"
```

```text
annotations.syn:1:1  [ERROR]  Field `region` (ON DATASET "interview.region") missing in the record `@silva2024`
```

**How to fix:** Complete the record, or make the field `OPTIONAL`.

# `QUESTIONS` and `EXPORT` blocks {#sec-blocos-projeto}

An error inside an `EXPORT` block shows as a **warning** at compile time and stops only that artifact in `synesis export`.

## E091 — Question without an identifier {#sec-e091}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `QuestionWithoutId`

A line of `QUESTIONS` does not have the form `<id>: <text>`.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    QUESTIONS
        Which barriers are reported?
    END QUESTIONS
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:7:9  [ERROR]  Question without identifier in QUESTIONS: `Which barriers are reported?` (use `Q1: text`)
```

**How to fix:** Write `Q1: text`.

## E092 — Question without text {#sec-e092}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `QuestionWithoutText`

There is an identifier without the question.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    QUESTIONS
        Q1:
    END QUESTIONS
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:7:9  [ERROR]  Question `Q1` without text in QUESTIONS
```

**How to fix:** Write the text after the colon.

## E093 — Repeated question identifier {#sec-e093}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `DuplicateQuestionId`

Two questions use the same identifier (case-insensitive).

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    QUESTIONS
        Q1: Which barriers are reported?
        q1: Which benefits are reported?
    END QUESTIONS
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:8:9  [ERROR]  Repeated question `q1` (first on line 7)
```

**How to fix:** Number them uniquely.

## E094 — Unknown `EXPORT` format {#sec-e094}

**Severity:** error local to the `EXPORT` block (warning at compile time) · **Class:** `UnknownExportFormat`

The accepted formats are `JSON`, `CSV`, `XLS`, `ALPACA`, `OKF` and `SKOS`.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    EXPORT PDF
        OUTPUT "out/report.pdf"
    END EXPORT
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:6:5  [WARNING]  EXPORT PDF: unknown format `PDF`
```

**How to fix:** Fix the format name.

## E095 — Unknown `EXPORT` property {#sec-e095}

**Severity:** error local to the `EXPORT` block (warning at compile time) · **Class:** `UnknownExportProperty`

The property is not accepted by that format.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    EXPORT CSV
        OUTPUT "out/csv"
        LANGUAGE en
    END EXPORT
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:8:9  [WARNING]  EXPORT CSV: unknown property `LANGUAGE` (accepted: OUTPUT, DESCRIPTION)
```

**How to fix:** See the properties of the format in the reference.

## E096 — Missing required property {#sec-e096}

**Severity:** error local to the `EXPORT` block (warning at compile time) · **Class:** `MissingExportProperty`

For instance `OUTPUT` (every format) or `NAMESPACE`/`LANGUAGE` (SKOS) is missing.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    EXPORT SKOS vocabulary
        OUTPUT "out/v.ttl"
    END EXPORT
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:6:5  [WARNING]  EXPORT SKOS vocabulary: required property `NAMESPACE` is missing
project.synp:6:5  [WARNING]  EXPORT SKOS vocabulary: required property `LANGUAGE` is missing
```

**How to fix:** Add the property.

## E097 — Repeated property {#sec-e097}

**Severity:** error local to the `EXPORT` block (warning at compile time) · **Class:** `DuplicateExportProperty`

The same property appears twice in the block.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    EXPORT JSON
        OUTPUT "out/a.json"
        OUTPUT "out/b.json"
    END EXPORT
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:8:9  [WARNING]  EXPORT JSON: repeated property `OUTPUT`
```

**How to fix:** Keep one.

## E098 — Ambiguous `EXPORT` blocks {#sec-e098}

**Severity:** error local to the `EXPORT` block (warning at compile time) · **Class:** `AmbiguousExportName`

Two unnamed blocks of the same format, repeated names, or a name equal to a format.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    EXPORT JSON
        OUTPUT "out/a.json"
    END EXPORT
    EXPORT JSON
        OUTPUT "out/b.json"
    END EXPORT
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:6:5  [WARNING]  EXPORT JSON: there are 2 JSON blocks and this one has no name
project.synp:9:5  [WARNING]  EXPORT JSON: there are 2 JSON blocks and this one has no name
```

**How to fix:** Give each block a distinct name.

## E099 — `MAP` in a format that does not use it {#sec-e099}

**Severity:** error local to the `EXPORT` block (warning at compile time) · **Class:** `MapNotSupported`

`MAP RELATIONS` exists only in SKOS; `MAP <fields> TO` only in ALPACA.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    EXPORT CSV
        OUTPUT "out/csv"
        MAP RELATIONS ENABLES TO RELATED
    END EXPORT
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:8:9  [WARNING]  EXPORT CSV: `MAP` is not accepted in this format
```

**How to fix:** Remove the line.

## E100 — Invalid `GENERATED_AT` {#sec-e100}

**Severity:** error local to the `EXPORT` block (warning at compile time) · **Class:** `InvalidGeneratedAt`

The date must be ISO 8601 **with a time zone**.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    EXPORT JSON
        OUTPUT "out/a.json"
        GENERATED_AT 2026-11-25
    END EXPORT
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:6:5  [WARNING]  EXPORT JSON: invalid GENERATED_AT `2026-11-25` (ISO 8601 with time zone)
```

**How to fix:** For instance `2026-11-25T00:00:00Z`.

# Roles and the organizing model {#sec-roles}

These diagnostics appear when the template gives ONTOLOGY fields a function with `ROLE`. See [The Organizing Model](organizing_model.qmd).

## E101 — Cited concept without a block {#sec-e101}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `UndeclaredConcept`

A `CODE` field of ONTOLOGY cites a concept that has no `ONTOLOGY` block.

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD kind_of TYPE CODE
    SCOPE ONTOLOGY
    ROLE HIERARCHY KIND
END FIELD
```

```synesis
# ontology.syno
ONTOLOGY smishing
    kind_of: phishing
END ONTOLOGY
```

```text
ontology.syno:2:5  [ERROR]  `kind_of`: concept `phishing` without an ONTOLOGY block (parecido: `smishing`)
```

**How to fix:** Create the block of the cited concept.

## E102 — Empty item in a list {#sec-e102}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `InvalidValueForm`

A list in an ONTOLOGY `CODE` field has an empty element.

```synesis
# ontology.syno
ONTOLOGY smishing
    kind_of: phishing, , fraud
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY phishing
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY fraud
END ONTOLOGY
```

```text
ontology.syno:2:5  [ERROR]  `kind_of`: empty item in the list
```

**How to fix:** Remove the extra comma.

## E104 — Unknown role {#sec-e104}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `UnknownRole`

The text after `ROLE` is not in the catalogue.

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD x TYPE TEXT
    SCOPE ONTOLOGY
    ROLE SYNONYM
END FIELD
```

```text
template.synt:11:1  [ERROR]  Unknown role `SYNONYM` in the field `x`
```

**How to fix:** Use a role from the catalogue (`LABEL`, `NOTE`, `HIERARCHY`, `USE`).

## E105 — Role not yet available {#sec-e105}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `RoleNotAvailable`

The role is planned (`DIVISION EXCLUSIVE` or `COMPLETE`) but not implemented yet.

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD x TYPE CODE
    SCOPE ONTOLOGY
    ROLE DIVISION EXCLUSIVE
END FIELD
```

```text
template.synt:11:1  [ERROR]  Role `DIVISION EXCLUSIVE` not yet available (field `x`)
```

**How to fix:** Remove the `ROLE` line.

## E106 — Role without a species {#sec-e106}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `RoleRequiresSpecies`

`LABEL`, `NOTE` and `HIERARCHY` require a species.

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD x TYPE CODE
    SCOPE ONTOLOGY
    ROLE HIERARCHY
END FIELD
```

```text
template.synt:11:1  [ERROR]  Role `HIERARCHY` without a species in the field `x`
```

**How to fix:** Write, for instance, `ROLE HIERARCHY KIND`.

## E107 — Type incompatible with the role {#sec-e107}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `RoleTypeMismatch`

`LABEL` and `NOTE` require `TEXT`; `HIERARCHY` and `USE` require `CODE`.

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD x TYPE TEXT
    SCOPE ONTOLOGY
    ROLE HIERARCHY KIND
END FIELD
```

```text
template.synt:11:1  [ERROR]  `x`: `HIERARCHY KIND` exige TYPE CODE (e TEXT)
```

**How to fix:** Change the `TYPE` of the field.

## E108 — `ROLE` outside `ONTOLOGY` {#sec-e108}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `RoleOutsideOntology`

Roles only exist in `SCOPE ONTOLOGY` fields.

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD x TYPE TEXT
    SCOPE ITEM
    ROLE NOTE DEFINITION
END FIELD
```

```text
template.synt:8:1  [ERROR]  ROLE NOTE DEFINITION in `x` (SCOPE ITEM): only valid in SCOPE ONTOLOGY
```

**How to fix:** Remove the `ROLE` line or change the scope.

## E109 — Repeated `ROLE` {#sec-e109}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `DuplicateRole`

The same `FIELD` declares two `ROLE` lines.

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD x TYPE TEXT
    SCOPE ONTOLOGY
    ROLE NOTE DEFINITION
    ROLE NOTE USAGE
END FIELD
```

```text
template.synt:11:1  [ERROR]  Repeated ROLE in the field `x`
```

**How to fix:** Keep one.

## E110 — Unique role in two fields {#sec-e110}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `DuplicateUniqueRole`

There can be only one `NOTE DEFINITION`, one `LABEL PREFERRED` and one `USE` field.

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD a TYPE TEXT
    SCOPE ONTOLOGY
    ROLE NOTE DEFINITION
END FIELD
```

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD b TYPE TEXT
    SCOPE ONTOLOGY
    ROLE NOTE DEFINITION
END FIELD
```

```text
template.synt:16:1  [ERROR]  `NOTE DEFINITION` in two fields: `a` and `b`
```

**How to fix:** Keep the role in a single field.

## E111 — Required hierarchy {#sec-e111}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `RequiredHierarchy`

A `HIERARCHY` field cannot be `REQUIRED`: top concepts have no parent.

```synesis
# template.synt
ITEM FIELDS
    REQUIRED quote
END ITEM FIELDS

ONTOLOGY FIELDS
    REQUIRED kind_of
END ONTOLOGY FIELDS
```

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD kind_of TYPE CODE
    SCOPE ONTOLOGY
    ROLE HIERARCHY KIND
END FIELD
```

```text
template.synt:11:1  [ERROR]  `kind_of` (HIERARCHY KIND) cannot be REQUIRED: the top concepts would be invalid
```

**How to fix:** List the field as `OPTIONAL`.

## E112 — Reserved field name {#sec-e112}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `ReservedOntologyFieldName`

An ONTOLOGY field uses a name that is a canonical key of the JSON.

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD frequency TYPE TEXT
    SCOPE ONTOLOGY
END FIELD
```

```text
template.synt:11:1  [ERROR]  ONTOLOGY field `frequency` uses a name reserved in the JSON
```

**How to fix:** Rename the field.

## E113 — More than one preferred label {#sec-e113}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `MultiplePreferredLabels`

A concept has two terms in `LABEL PREFERRED`.

```synesis
# ontology.syno
ONTOLOGY smishing
    label: Smishing, SMS phishing
END ONTOLOGY
```

```text
ontology.syno:1:1  [ERROR]  `smishing`: more than one preferred label
```

**How to fix:** Keep one; move the others to a `LABEL ALTERNATIVE` field.

## E114 — Term in two label species {#sec-e114}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `LabelSpeciesOverlap`

The same term is in two `LABEL` fields of the same concept.

```synesis
# ontology.syno
ONTOLOGY smishing
    used_for: SMS phishing
    old_name: SMS phishing
END ONTOLOGY
```

```text
ontology.syno:1:1  [ERROR]  `smishing`: `SMS phishing` in two LABEL species
```

**How to fix:** Keep the term in one of them.

## E115 — Ambiguous label {#sec-e115}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `AmbiguousLabel`

The same term labels two concepts.

```synesis
# ontology.syno
ONTOLOGY smishing
    used_for: text scam
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY vishing
    used_for: text scam
END ONTOLOGY
```

```text
ontology.syno:5:1  [ERROR]  Label `text scam` on two concepts: `smishing` and `vishing`
```

**How to fix:** A label belongs to a single concept.

## E116 — Label equal to another concept {#sec-e116}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `LabelConflictsWithConcept`

A label matches the name of another concept.

```synesis
# ontology.syno
ONTOLOGY smishing
    used_for: vishing
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY vishing
END ONTOLOGY
```

```text
ontology.syno:1:1  [ERROR]  `smishing`: label `vishing` is the name of the concept `vishing`
```

**How to fix:** Remove the label or consolidate the concepts with `USE`.

## E117 — Self-reference in the hierarchy {#sec-e117}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `SelfReference`

A concept is given as its own parent.

```synesis
# ontology.syno
ONTOLOGY phishing
    kind_of: phishing
END ONTOLOGY
```

```text
ontology.syno:1:1  [ERROR]  `phishing` points to itself in `kind_of`
```

**How to fix:** Point to the broader concept.

## E118 — Cycle in the hierarchy {#sec-e118}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `CyclicHierarchy`

Following the parents leads back to the starting concept.

```synesis
# ontology.syno
ONTOLOGY phishing
    kind_of: smishing
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY smishing
    kind_of: phishing
END ONTOLOGY
```

```text
ontology.syno:1:1  [ERROR]  Hierarchy cycle: phishing -> smishing -> phishing
```

**How to fix:** Break the cycle. The prohibition is a Synesis rule.

## E119 — Pair in two hierarchy species {#sec-e119}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `DuplicateHierarchySpecies`

The same child-parent pair appears in two `HIERARCHY` fields.

```synesis
# ontology.syno
ONTOLOGY smishing
    kind_of: phishing
    part_of: phishing
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY phishing
END ONTOLOGY
```

```text
ontology.syno:1:1  [ERROR]  `smishing` -> `phishing` in two species (KIND, PART)
```

**How to fix:** Choose one species.

## E120 — Ungrounded concept {#sec-e120}

**Severity:** warning · **Class:** `UngroundedConcept`

The block is mentioned by no ITEM and has no mentioned descendant.

```synesis
# ontology.syno
ONTOLOGY phishing
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY smishing
    kind_of: phishing
END ONTOLOGY
```

```text
ontology.syno:1:1  [WARNING]  `phishing` has no mention and no mentioned descendant
ontology.syno:4:1  [WARNING]  `smishing` has no mention and no mentioned descendant
```

**How to fix:** Code evidence for the concept or remove the block.

## E121 — Hierarchy by field name (deprecated) {#sec-e121}

**Severity:** warning · **Class:** `DeprecatedNameBasedHierarchy`

The hierarchy was read from the name `parent`/`is_a`, a deprecated route.

```synesis
# template.synt
FIELD parent TYPE CHAIN
    SCOPE ONTOLOGY
    ARITY >= 2
END FIELD
```

```synesis
# ontology.syno
ONTOLOGY smishing
    parent: smishing -> phishing
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY phishing
END ONTOLOGY
```

```text
ontology.syno:1:1  [WARNING]  `smishing`: hierarchy by the name `parent` (deprecated route)
```

**How to fix:** Declare `ROLE HIERARCHY` on the field.

# Consolidating names (`ROLE USE`) {#sec-use}

## E145 — `USE` pointing to itself {#sec-e145}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `UseSelf`

The deprecated block points to itself.

```synesis
# ontology.syno
ONTOLOGY vishing
    use: vishing
END ONTOLOGY
```

```text
ontology.syno:1:1  [ERROR]  `vishing` uses itself in `use`
```

**How to fix:** Point to the concept that holds.

## E146 — Chained `USE` {#sec-e146}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `UseChain`

The target is deprecated too.

```synesis
# ontology.syno
ONTOLOGY voice_scam
    use: voice_phishing
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY voice_phishing
    use: vishing
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY vishing
END ONTOLOGY
```

```text
ontology.syno:1:1  [ERROR]  `voice_scam` uses `voice_phishing`, which uses `vishing`
```

**How to fix:** Point directly to the concept that holds.

## E147 — `USE` with several targets {#sec-e147}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `UseMultipleTargets`

A deprecated name stands for a single concept.

```synesis
# ontology.syno
ONTOLOGY voice_phishing
    use: vishing, phishing
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY vishing
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY phishing
END ONTOLOGY
```

```text
ontology.syno:1:1  [ERROR]  `voice_phishing`: USE with several targets (vishing, phishing)
```

**How to fix:** Give a single target.

## E148 — Deprecated block with other fields {#sec-e148}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `AliasWithContent`

A block with `USE` holds no other field.

```synesis
# ontology.syno
ONTOLOGY voice_phishing
    use: vishing
    used_for: voice scam
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY vishing
END ONTOLOGY
```

```text
ontology.syno:1:1  [ERROR]  `voice_phishing` is an alias and has other fields (used_for)
```

**How to fix:** Keep only `USE`; `synesis-coder consolidate` moves the rest.

## E149 — Hierarchy collapsing after `USE` {#sec-e149}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `HierarchyCollapsedByUse`

Once deprecated names are resolved, a concept would be its own parent.

```synesis
# ontology.syno
ONTOLOGY voice_phishing
    use: vishing
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY vishing
    kind_of: voice_phishing
END ONTOLOGY
```

```text
ontology.syno:5:1  [ERROR]  `vishing` -> `voice_phishing` collapses after USE (parent of itself)
```

**How to fix:** Remove the hierarchical link between the two names.

# Production plan (`PHASE`) {#sec-phase}

The compiler only validates the plan; the phases are run by `synesis-coder`.

## E133 — Unknown phase property {#sec-e133}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `UnknownPhaseProperty`

The properties are `FIELDS`, `INPUT`, `RULES` and `OUTPUT` (the last only in `ONTOLOGY`).

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    PHASE ONTOLOGY defs
        FIELDS definition
        MODEL claude
    END PHASE
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:8:9  [ERROR]  PHASE ONTOLOGY defs: unknown property `MODEL`
```

**How to fix:** Fix the property.

## E134 — Repeated phase property {#sec-e134}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `DuplicatePhaseProperty`

The same property appears twice.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    PHASE ONTOLOGY defs
        FIELDS definition
        FIELDS topic
    END PHASE
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:8:9  [ERROR]  PHASE ONTOLOGY defs: repeated property `FIELDS`
```

**How to fix:** Keep one.

## E135 — Phase without fields {#sec-e135}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `EmptyPhaseList`

`FIELDS` is missing, or a list is empty.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    PHASE ONTOLOGY defs
        INPUT quote
    END PHASE
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:6:5  [ERROR]  PHASE ONTOLOGY defs: `FIELDS` without fields
```

**How to fix:** List the fields the phase produces.

## E136 — Phase field outside the template {#sec-e136}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `UnknownPhaseField`

The phase cites a field the template does not define.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    PHASE ONTOLOGY defs
        FIELDS meaning
    END PHASE
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:6:5  [ERROR]  PHASE ONTOLOGY defs: field `meaning` (FIELDS) outside the template
```

**How to fix:** Fix the name.

## E137 — Field in two phases {#sec-e137}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `FieldInTwoPhases`

Each field is produced by a single phase.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    PHASE ONTOLOGY a
        FIELDS definition
    END PHASE
    PHASE ONTOLOGY b
        FIELDS definition
    END PHASE
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:9:5  [ERROR]  PHASE ONTOLOGY b: `definition` is already produced by `PHASE ONTOLOGY a`
```

**How to fix:** Remove it from one of them.

## E138 — Field of another scope {#sec-e138}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `PhaseScopeMismatch`

A `PHASE ONTOLOGY` only produces ONTOLOGY fields.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    PHASE ONTOLOGY defs
        FIELDS quote
    END PHASE
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:6:5  [ERROR]  PHASE ONTOLOGY defs: `quote` (ITEM) outside the phase scope
```

**How to fix:** Move the field or change the phase scope.

## E139 — Input produced only later {#sec-e139}

**Severity:** warning · **Class:** `InputNotAvailable`

The `INPUT` depends on a field that only a later phase produces.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    PHASE ONTOLOGY a
        FIELDS definition
        INPUT topic
    END PHASE
    PHASE ONTOLOGY b
        FIELDS topic
    END PHASE
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:6:5  [WARNING]  PHASE ONTOLOGY a: INPUT `topic` only produced by a later phase
```

**How to fix:** Reorder the phases.

## E140 — Bundle split across phases {#sec-e140}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `BundleSplitAcrossPhases`

Fields of one `BUNDLE` are in different phases.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    PHASE ONTOLOGY a
        FIELDS definition
    END PHASE
    PHASE ONTOLOGY b
        FIELDS topic
    END PHASE
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:6:5  [ERROR]  BUNDLE (definition, topic) split across phases
```

**How to fix:** Put them all in the same phase.

## E141 — Required field without a phase {#sec-e141}

**Severity:** warning · **Class:** `FieldWithoutPhase`

There are `PHASE` blocks but none produces a `REQUIRED` field of the covered scope.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    PHASE ONTOLOGY a
        FIELDS definition
    END PHASE
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:1:1  [WARNING]  REQUIRED field `topic` without a phase
```

**How to fix:** Include the field in a phase.

## E142 — Ambiguous destination {#sec-e142}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `AmbiguousPhaseOutput`

The phase declares no `OUTPUT` and the project does not have exactly one eligible local `.syno`.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "extra.syno"
    PHASE ONTOLOGY a
        FIELDS definition
    END PHASE
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:7:5  [ERROR]  PHASE ONTOLOGY a: ambiguous destination (2 eligible .syno files); use OUTPUT
```

**How to fix:** Declare `OUTPUT "file.syno"`.

## E143 — `OUTPUT` that is not a local `.syno` {#sec-e143}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `PhaseOutputNotLocal`

The destination must be a `.syno` of the project cited as a file.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    PHASE ONTOLOGY a
        FIELDS definition
        OUTPUT "out/file.json"
    END PHASE
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:6:5  [ERROR]  PHASE ONTOLOGY a: OUTPUT `out/file.json` is not a local .syno of the project
```

**How to fix:** Point to an included `.syno`.

## E144 — Colliding phase names {#sec-e144}

**Severity:** error · **Class:** `PhaseNameCollision`

Two phases share a name, or names that yield the same environment variable.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    PHASE ONTOLOGY syn-a
        FIELDS definition
    END PHASE
    PHASE ONTOLOGY syn_a
        FIELDS topic
    END PHASE
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:9:5  [ERROR]  PHASE ONTOLOGY syn_a collides with PHASE ONTOLOGY syn-a (same environment variable)
```

**How to fix:** Rename a phase.

# SKOS export {#sec-skos}

## E122 — Unknown relation in `MAP RELATIONS` {#sec-e122}

**Severity:** error local to the `EXPORT` block (warning at compile time) · **Class:** `UnknownRelation`

The relation is not in the `RELATIONS` of any `CHAIN` field.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    EXPORT SKOS vocabulary
        OUTPUT "out/v.ttl"
        NAMESPACE "https://example.org/id/demo/"
        LANGUAGE en
        MAP RELATIONS PART_OF TO HIERARCHY PART
    END EXPORT
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:10:9  [WARNING]  EXPORT SKOS vocabulary: unknown relation `PART_OF`
```

**How to fix:** Use the name declared in the template.

## E123 — Ambiguous relation {#sec-e123}

**Severity:** error local to the `EXPORT` block (warning at compile time) · **Class:** `AmbiguousRelation`

The relation exists in more than one `CHAIN` field.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    EXPORT SKOS vocabulary
        OUTPUT "out/v.ttl"
        NAMESPACE "https://example.org/id/demo/"
        LANGUAGE en
        MAP RELATIONS KIND_OF TO HIERARCHY KIND
    END EXPORT
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:10:9  [WARNING]  EXPORT SKOS vocabulary: `KIND_OF` in several CHAIN fields; use FROM
```

**How to fix:** Name the field with `FROM <field>`.

## E124 — Target not accepted in `MAP RELATIONS` {#sec-e124}

**Severity:** error local to the `EXPORT` block (warning at compile time) · **Class:** `MapTargetNotAllowed`

The targets are `HIERARCHY KIND`, `HIERARCHY PART`, `HIERARCHY INSTANCE` and `RELATED`.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    EXPORT SKOS vocabulary
        OUTPUT "out/v.ttl"
        NAMESPACE "https://example.org/id/demo/"
        LANGUAGE en
        MAP RELATIONS KIND_OF TO BROADER
    END EXPORT
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:10:9  [WARNING]  EXPORT SKOS vocabulary: target `BROADER` not accepted in MAP RELATIONS
```

**How to fix:** Use one of these targets.

## E125 — Relation mapped twice {#sec-e125}

**Severity:** error local to the `EXPORT` block (warning at compile time) · **Class:** `RelationMappedTwice`

The same relation appears in two `MAP RELATIONS` lines of the block.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    EXPORT SKOS vocabulary
        OUTPUT "out/v.ttl"
        NAMESPACE "https://example.org/id/demo/"
        LANGUAGE en
        MAP RELATIONS KIND_OF TO HIERARCHY KIND
        MAP RELATIONS KIND_OF TO RELATED
    END EXPORT
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:11:9  [WARNING]  EXPORT SKOS vocabulary: relation `KIND_OF` mapped twice
```

**How to fix:** Map each relation once.

## E126 — Invalid `MIN_SOURCES` {#sec-e126}

**Severity:** error local to the `EXPORT` block (warning at compile time) · **Class:** `InvalidMinSources`

The value must be an integer of 1 or more.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    EXPORT SKOS vocabulary
        OUTPUT "out/v.ttl"
        NAMESPACE "https://example.org/id/demo/"
        LANGUAGE en
        MIN_SOURCES 0
    END EXPORT
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:6:5  [WARNING]  EXPORT SKOS vocabulary: invalid MIN_SOURCES `0`
```

**How to fix:** Fix the number.

## E127 — Invalid `NAMESPACE` {#sec-e127}

**Severity:** error local to the `EXPORT` block (warning at compile time) · **Class:** `InvalidNamespace`

It must be an absolute IRI ending in `/` or `#`.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    EXPORT SKOS vocabulary
        OUTPUT "out/v.ttl"
        NAMESPACE "demo"
        LANGUAGE en
    END EXPORT
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:6:5  [WARNING]  EXPORT SKOS vocabulary: invalid NAMESPACE `demo`
```

**How to fix:** Use a domain the team controls.

## E128 — Invalid `LANGUAGE` {#sec-e128}

**Severity:** error local to the `EXPORT` block (warning at compile time) · **Class:** `InvalidLanguageTag`

It must be a well-formed BCP 47 tag, such as `pt-BR` or `en`.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    EXPORT SKOS vocabulary
        OUTPUT "out/v.ttl"
        NAMESPACE "https://example.org/id/demo/"
        LANGUAGE portugues_br
    END EXPORT
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:6:5  [WARNING]  EXPORT SKOS vocabulary: invalid LANGUAGE `portugues_br`
```

**How to fix:** Fix the tag.

## E129 — Conflicting derived label {#sec-e129}

**Severity:** error local to the `EXPORT` block (warning at compile time) · **Class:** `DerivedLabelConflict`

Without `LABEL PREFERRED`, the preferred label is the block name with `_` replaced by a space; it matches a label of another concept.

```synesis
# ontology.syno
ONTOLOGY text_scam
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY smishing
    used_for: text scam
END ONTOLOGY
```

```text
project.synp:6:5  [ERROR]  EXPORT SKOS vocabulary: derived label "text scam" of `text_scam` matches `smishing`
```

**How to fix:** Change the other label or declare a preferred label.

## E130 — Derived label repeated in the same concept {#sec-e130}

**Severity:** error local to the `EXPORT` block (warning at compile time) · **Class:** `DerivedLabelOverlap`

The label derived from the name matches an alternative or hidden label of the same concept (SKOS condition S13).

```synesis
# ontology.syno
ONTOLOGY text_scam
    used_for: text scam
END ONTOLOGY
```

```text
project.synp:6:5  [ERROR]  EXPORT SKOS vocabulary: "text scam" is both preferred and alternative in `text_scam`
project.synp:6:5  [ERROR]  EXPORT SKOS vocabulary: SKOS integrity S13 (1)
```

**How to fix:** Remove the redundant term.

## E131 — Repeated IRI {#sec-e131}

**Severity:** error local to the `EXPORT` block (warning at compile time) · **Class:** `IriCollision`

Two resources would get the same IRI. It is a defensive check, not expected to show.

**How to fix:** Rename one of the concepts.

## E132 — Merged `TOPIC` spellings {#sec-e132}

**Severity:** warning · **Class:** `TopicCaseVariant`

`TOPIC` values differing only in spelling are merged into one collection. It is a warning.

```synesis
# ontology.syno
ONTOLOGY phishing
    topic: Fraud
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY smishing
    topic: fraud
END ONTOLOGY
```

```text
  ⚠ Warnings (1):
    TOPIC spellings merged:
      • (Fraud, fraud) -> "Fraud"
```

**How to fix:** Standardize the spelling in the `.syno`.

## E150 — Unknown `ALIAS_LABEL` {#sec-e150}

**Severity:** error local to the `EXPORT` block (warning at compile time) · **Class:** `UnknownAliasLabel`

The accepted values are `HIDDEN` and `ALTERNATIVE`.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    EXPORT SKOS vocabulary
        OUTPUT "out/v.ttl"
        NAMESPACE "https://example.org/id/demo/"
        LANGUAGE en
        ALIAS_LABEL VISIBLE
    END EXPORT
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:6:5  [ERROR]  EXPORT SKOS vocabulary: unknown ALIAS_LABEL `VISIBLE`
```

**How to fix:** Fix the value.

## E151 — Deprecated name equal to a label {#sec-e151}

**Severity:** error local to the `EXPORT` block (warning at compile time) · **Class:** `AliasLabelCollision`

The deprecated name (`USE`) is already a label of the target.

```synesis
# ontology.syno
ONTOLOGY voice_phishing
    use: vishing
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY vishing
    used_for: voice phishing
END ONTOLOGY
```

```text
  ⚠ Warnings (1):
    `voice_phishing` is already a label of `vishing`
```

**How to fix:** Remove the duplicate label.

## E152 — Unusable `REGISTRY` {#sec-e152}

**Severity:** error local to the `EXPORT` block (warning at compile time) · **Class:** `RegistryNotFound`

The registry does not exist or is not a readable text file. With `--publish` it is an error and nothing is written.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    EXPORT SKOS vocabulary
        OUTPUT "out/v.ttl"
        NAMESPACE "https://example.org/id/demo/"
        LANGUAGE en
        REGISTRY "registry"
    END EXPORT
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:6:5  [ERROR]  EXPORT SKOS vocabulary: REGISTRY `registry` unusable
```

**How to fix:** Point to a text file (it is created on the first publication).

## E153 — Published IRI without a successor {#sec-e153}

**Severity:** warning; error with `--publish` · **Class:** `PublishedIriWithoutBlock`

An IRI in the `REGISTRY` matches no block and no `USE`. With `--publish` it is an error: a published IRI never vanishes.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    EXPORT SKOS vocabulary
        OUTPUT "out/v.ttl"
        NAMESPACE "https://example.org/id/demo/"
        LANGUAGE en
        REGISTRY "iris.txt"
    END EXPORT
END PROJECT
```

```text
  ⚠ Warnings (1):
    Published IRI without a block:
      • `https://example.org/id/demo/concept/voice_scam`
```

**How to fix:** Restore the block or declare `USE` pointing to the successor.

## E154 — SKOS integrity violation {#sec-e154}

**Severity:** error local to the `EXPORT` block (warning at compile time) · **Class:** `SkosIntegrityViolation`

The generated graph breaks a SKOS integrity condition (S9, S13, S14, S27, S37) or the Synesis rule against cycles. The file is not written.

**How to fix:** Revise the labels and hierarchy named in the message.

## E155 — SKOS quality notice {#sec-e155}

**Severity:** warning · **Class:** `SkosQualityNotice`

Editorial warning about the generated graph: resource without a preferred label, label without a language, concept with no position in the hierarchy or scheme without a top concept. The file is written.

**How to fix:** Complete the organizing model when relevant.
