## E156 — Registry IRIs outside the `NAMESPACE` {#sec-e156}

**Severity:** warning · **Class:** `RegistryOutsideNamespace`

The `REGISTRY` holds IRIs of another namespace, which are not checked. Changing the namespace is the researcher's decision.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    EXPORT SKOS vocabulary
        OUTPUT "out/v.ttl"
        NAMESPACE "https://example.org/id/demo/"
        LANGUAGE en
        REGISTRY "iris.txt"
    END EXPORT
END PROJECT
```

```text
  ⚠ Warnings (1):
    REGISTRY IRIs outside the NAMESPACE (not checked):
      • 1 — e.g. https://old.example.org/concept/vishing
```

**How to fix:** Redirect the old addresses if they are already in circulation.

## E157 — `OUTPUT` and `REGISTRY` on the same file {#sec-e157}

**Severity:** error local to the `EXPORT` block (warning at compile time) · **Class:** `RegistryIsOutput`

One would overwrite the other; the export is refused.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    EXPORT SKOS vocabulary
        OUTPUT "out/v.ttl"
        NAMESPACE "https://example.org/id/demo/"
        LANGUAGE en
        REGISTRY "out/v.ttl"
    END EXPORT
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:6:5  [ERROR]  EXPORT SKOS vocabulary: OUTPUT and REGISTRY are the same file `out\v.ttl`
```

**How to fix:** Use different files.

# Alpaca export {#sec-alpaca}

These diagnostics apply to `EXPORT ALPACA` blocks. Each one stops only the artifact of its block; the notices I166 and I167 stop nothing.

## E158 — Missing `MAP ... TO OUTPUT` {#sec-e158}

**Severity:** error local to the `EXPORT` block (warning at compile time) · **Class:** `AlpacaOutputMapMissing`

In declared mode you must say what goes in the output.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    EXPORT ALPACA training
        OUTPUT "out/t.jsonl"
        INSTRUCTION Identify the relation.
        MAP quote TO INPUT
    END EXPORT
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:6:5  [WARNING]  EXPORT ALPACA training: missing `MAP <fields> TO OUTPUT`
```

**How to fix:** Add `MAP <fields> TO OUTPUT`.

## E159 — Missing or double instruction source {#sec-e159}

**Severity:** error local to the `EXPORT` block (warning at compile time) · **Class:** `AlpacaInstructionSource`

There is exactly one source: the `INSTRUCTION` text or `MAP <field> TO INSTRUCTION`.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    EXPORT ALPACA training
        OUTPUT "out/t.jsonl"
        MAP chain TO OUTPUT
        MAP quote TO INPUT
    END EXPORT
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:6:5  [WARNING]  EXPORT ALPACA training: no instruction (INSTRUCTION <text> or MAP <field> TO INSTRUCTION)
```

**How to fix:** Declare only one.

## E160 — Unknown field in `MAP` {#sec-e160}

**Severity:** error local to the `EXPORT` block (warning at compile time) · **Class:** `AlpacaUnknownField`

The field is not in the template. The message suggests a similar name.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    EXPORT ALPACA training
        OUTPUT "out/t.jsonl"
        INSTRUCTION Identify the relation.
        MAP quot TO INPUT
        MAP chain TO OUTPUT
    END EXPORT
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:9:9  [WARNING]  EXPORT ALPACA training: unknown field `quot` (did you mean `quote`?)
```

**How to fix:** Fix the name.

## E161 — Field repeated in a target {#sec-e161}

**Severity:** error local to the `EXPORT` block (warning at compile time) · **Class:** `AlpacaDuplicateField`

The field was mapped twice to the same target.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    EXPORT ALPACA training
        OUTPUT "out/t.jsonl"
        INSTRUCTION Identify the relation.
        MAP quote, quote TO INPUT
        MAP chain TO OUTPUT
    END EXPORT
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:9:9  [WARNING]  EXPORT ALPACA training: `quote` mapped twice to INPUT
```

**How to fix:** List it once.

## E162 — Leak: field in output and input {#sec-e162}

**Severity:** error local to the `EXPORT` block (warning at compile time) · **Class:** `AlpacaFieldLeak`

An `OUTPUT` field is also in `INPUT` or `INSTRUCTION`; the answer would appear in the prompt.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    EXPORT ALPACA training
        OUTPUT "out/t.jsonl"
        INSTRUCTION Identify the relation.
        MAP quote, chain TO INPUT
        MAP chain TO OUTPUT
    END EXPORT
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:6:5  [WARNING]  EXPORT ALPACA training: `chain` in OUTPUT and in INPUT (answer leaks into the prompt)
```

**How to fix:** Separate the fields.

## E163 — Fields from two bundles {#sec-e163}

**Severity:** error local to the `EXPORT` block (warning at compile time) · **Class:** `AlpacaMultipleBundles`

Each line needs a single unit.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    EXPORT ALPACA training
        OUTPUT "out/t.jsonl"
        INSTRUCTION Identify the relation.
        MAP chain TO INPUT
        MAP note TO OUTPUT
    END EXPORT
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:6:5  [WARNING]  EXPORT ALPACA training: fields from 2 bundles; use fields of one BUNDLE
```

**How to fix:** Use fields of one bundle per block; create another block for the second.

## E164 — Field not supported yet {#sec-e164}

**Severity:** error local to the `EXPORT` block (warning at compile time) · **Class:** `AlpacaFieldNotSupported`

ONTOLOGY fields and SOURCE fields with `ON BIBLIOGRAPHY`/`ON DATASET` cannot enter the map.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    EXPORT ALPACA training
        OUTPUT "out/t.jsonl"
        INSTRUCTION Identify the relation.
        MAP definition TO INPUT
        MAP chain TO OUTPUT
    END EXPORT
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:9:9  [WARNING]  EXPORT ALPACA training: `definition` not supported yet (ONTOLOGY field)
```

**How to fix:** Remove the field.

## E165 — Invalid `MAP` target {#sec-e165}

**Severity:** error local to the `EXPORT` block (warning at compile time) · **Class:** `AlpacaMapTarget`

The targets are `INSTRUCTION`, `INPUT` and `OUTPUT`, without `FROM`.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    EXPORT ALPACA training
        OUTPUT "out/t.jsonl"
        INSTRUCTION Identify the relation.
        MAP quote TO PROMPT
        MAP chain TO OUTPUT
    END EXPORT
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:9:9  [WARNING]  EXPORT ALPACA training: target `PROMPT` not accepted (INSTRUCTION, INPUT, OUTPUT)
```

**How to fix:** Fix the target.

## I166 — Qualifier left out of the map {#sec-i166}

**Severity:** notice · **Class:** `AlpacaBundlePartnerOmitted`

A field that qualifies the bundle (for instance the status of a relation) was left out. The file is written.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    EXPORT ALPACA training
        OUTPUT "out/t.jsonl"
        INSTRUCTION Identify the relation.
        MAP quote TO INPUT
        MAP chain TO OUTPUT
    END EXPORT
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:6:5  [INFO]  EXPORT ALPACA training: `status` qualifies `chain` in the BUNDLE and is not in the dataset
```

**How to fix:** If the qualifier matters for training, add it to `OUTPUT`.

## I167 — Built-in pairs drop the qualifier {#sec-i167}

**Severity:** notice · **Class:** `AlpacaLegacyDropsQualifier`

Without `MAP`, the built-in pairs do not carry the qualifier of the CHAIN bundle, and a hypothesis comes out as an assertion.

```synesis
# project.synp
PROJECT demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"
    EXPORT ALPACA training
        OUTPUT "out/t.jsonl"
    END EXPORT
END PROJECT
```

```text
project.synp:6:5  [INFO]  EXPORT ALPACA training: built-in pairs drop `status` (qualifies `chain`); declare MAP ... TO OUTPUT
```

**How to fix:** Declare `MAP ... TO OUTPUT` including the qualifier.

# Syntax errors {#sec-sintaxe}

When the text does not follow the grammar, the compiler never reaches validation and there is no semantic code: the message shows where reading stopped (`Unexpected token`) and what was expected. In an included file it comes wrapped in [E076](#sec-e076); in the `.synp` or the template, in [E064](#sec-e064).

The most common causes:

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| error right after the template name | `version:` or `author:` on its own line | write them on the same line: `TEMPLATE name version: "1.0"` |
| error inside the `VALUES` of an `ORDERED` | index without brackets (`1 low:`) | write `[1] low: ...` |
| `Unexpected token <EOF>` | an `END ...` is missing | close every block |
| error in a multi-line value | continuation without indentation | indent the following lines more than the field name |
| error in the `.synp` | indented blocks mixed with blocks at column 0 | indent all the content of `PROJECT` consistently |
